name: delegated-build
description: Implement with the result-block evidence discipline, then hand delivery to no-mistakes, which owns review, fixes, tests, documentation, push, PR and CI. No independent QA or review step: nothing here is a second reviewer on top of no-mistakes.
when: A code-changing task whose selected delivery path is no-mistakes. The orchestration, evidence record and change-direction outcome still apply, but review and testing belong to no-mistakes alone: this workflow adds no manual reviewer or gate on top of it.

direction.description: A change of direction was raised and the orchestrator chose to reshape: implement again, at most twice.

implement.instruction: Implement the task. Read the project instructions and its verify convention first; work in thin verifiable slices; run the project cheap checks and the real flow end to end and show what they printed. Commit to the task branch and report with the result block: base and commit, the evidence, what you could not verify. Review, testing, documentation, push, PR and CI belong to the delivery path that follows (no-mistakes): add no reviewer or gate of your own. If the plan or approach cannot meet the acceptance, stop early with status change-direction and the evidence.

deliver.instruction: The implementation is committed. Deliver through no-mistakes, the selected delivery path: it owns review, fixes, tests, documentation, push, PR and CI. Add no reviewer or gate of your own and do not hold the work for a manual verdict. The verification stamp below is what the implementer ran; for the rest say: review and testing owned by no-mistakes. Never merge.

redirect.question: A worker, reviewer or the plan reported that the approach itself is wrong (change-direction). Reshape and re-plan, close the task, or escalate?
criteria: reshape: the reported direction is another route to the SAME authorized outcome - no wider scope, no new authority, no extra cost. The reshaped approach goes back in as input; this is not a licence to retry the old approach.
close: the goal is unreachable, no longer worth it, or already satisfied. Closing is cheap - the code was fast to write. Report why.
escalate: the direction changes scope, acceptance, authority, risk or cost, or this is the second reshape: the captain decides.
Never choose reshape to avoid closing, and never grind on a plan the evidence says is wrong. Record the reason; it is kept in the workflow state.
